titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spells 44, 45, 46, 50 and 93
about: Five short spells on Plates 16 and 17 of Ani's papyrus, written after Spells 58 and 59. Each keeps the dead man whole in the world below: not dying a second time (Spell 44), not rotting (Spell 45), not perishing (Spell 46), not coming to the slaughter-block of the gods (Spell 50), and not being ferried off to the east to the festivals of the rebels (Spell 93, followed by another spell to the same end). Ani speaks as Ra, as Osiris and as the son of Osiris, and names the parts of his body that are made firm. The words are short and often obscure, many signs in Budge's print are uncertain, and the notes say where a reading is doubtful.

sentences.l: spell · of · not · dying · again · in · the-necropolis
sentences.i: Spell for not dying again in the necropolis.
sentences.n: Spell 44 begins. The papyrus writes rꜣ n tmt mt m nm in red, and m ẖrt-nṯr in black. rꜣ n tmt 'spell for not …' as in the spells before: the mouth with its stroke, water n, and t, the sledge tm (U15) with the owl m as complement and a second t (Budge: temt), the negative verb tm, whose verb follows in the negatival complement. mt 'dying' is the owl m and t with a small ring printed under the t (coded N33, approximate), here a classifier not identified: the verb mwt 'die', written without its w. m nm is the owl m, then a slender slanting rod, taken as the knife nm (T34, approximate), the owl m as complement and the papyrus roll: m nm 'again, a second time', an adverbial phrase whose make-up is not clear (Budge: em nem). If the rod is the ox-leg (F25), the scribe meant m wḥm 'anew', with the same sense. ẖrt-nṯr 'the necropolis' is the flag nṯr, written first out of respect, the loop r (coded D21, approximate) and the block ẖr (T28). To die a second time was to be destroyed in the world below after the first death on earth: the end the dead most feared.

sentences.l: said · by · the-Osiris · Ani · is-opened · cavern-my · (twice)
sentences.i: Said by the Osiris Ani: My cavern is opened. (Twice.)
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in in red. ḏd in N 'said by N', as before: the cobra and the hand, then in, here the sign in (coded W25, approximate) with water n as complement. wsir is the low seat (coded Q2, approximate) over the eye, and ꜣny has the kneeling man with an arm raised as classifier. wnw is the hare wn (E34) with water n as complement, the chick w, and the hatched door (O31) over the low hooked sign (U15) as classifiers: the passive sḏm, 'is opened', with the w that the passive sometimes shows (Budge: unu). tpḥt·i 'my cavern' is p and t (the t printed under the p but read before it), the wick ḥ and t, a small house (coded O1, approximate) as classifier, and ·i. sp sn, the threshing floor sp and two strokes, tells the reader to say the words twice. The cavern is the tomb or the hollow of the world below: when it opens, the dead man can go out and in.

sentences.l: fall · the-spirits · within · the-darkness
sentences.i: The spirits fall within the darkness.
sentences.n: ḫr 'fall' is ḫ and r with a falling man (coded A15, approximate) as classifier, as in Spell 29: the sḏm·f, with its noun subject after it. ꜣḫw is the crested ibis ꜣḫ (G25) with ḫ as complement, the chick w and a dotted stroke (coded Z1): taken as the plural ꜣḫw 'spirits'. Budge reads 'light'; a word for light is written with the same ibis, but it usually has the sun as classifier, which is not printed here. The reading is doubtful. m ẖnw 'within' is the owl m and ẖnw 'the inside': the belly of an animal ẖ (F32), water n, the pot nw (W24) and the chick w, with a small house (coded O1, approximate). kkw 'darkness' is k twice and the chick w, with two strokes, not read, and the sky with a star hanging from it, the sign of night. Spirits or light, it is the night of the world below in which the speaker finds himself.

sentences.l: makes-known(?) · me · the-Eye · of-Horus
sentences.i: The Eye of Horus makes me known(?).
sentences.n: Budge prints seru-à as one group; it is split here into sr and wi (q re-indexed). The first sign of sr is uncertain: a low flat sign with a ring at one end and an upright at the other, coded as the sledge U15; Budge reads s, and the reading follows him. Then the mouth r and the papyrus roll, the classifier of things abstract: sr 'make known, foretell', a sḏm·f whose noun subject irt ḥr 'the Eye of Horus' comes at the end. wi, the chick w and the seated man, is the dependent pronoun 'me', which stands before a noun subject. Budge has 'hath arranged me'; the sense of sr here is doubtful. irt 'eye' is the eye ir with t and a stroke, and ḥr 'Horus' is the falcon alone. The Eye of Horus, torn out by Seth and made whole again, stands for every restoring of what was damaged.

sentences.l: has-nursed · me · Wepwawet
sentences.i: Wepwawet has nursed me.
sentences.n: Budge prints renen-nuà as one group; it is split here into rnn·n and wi (q re-indexed; the water n and the chick, printed one over the other, now fall in different words). rnn 'nurse, bring up' is the mouth r and water n twice, with a kneeling woman holding a child (coded B5, approximate) as classifier; the third water n is the n of the sḏm·n·f, 'has nursed'. wi 'me' again comes before the noun subject. wp-wꜣwt 'Opener of the Ways' is the horns wp (F13), the road with shrubs wꜣ (coded N31, approximate), t and two strokes, and the jackal on its standard as classifier (Budge: Àp-uat). Wepwawet, a jackal god like Anubis, goes before the dead and opens their roads.

sentences.l: has-hidden · me · with-you · Imperishable-Stars
sentences.i: He has hidden me in your keeping, you Imperishable Stars.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes iw ḫmw sk; read iḫmw-sk. Budge prints àmen-nuà as one group; it is split here into imn·n and wi (q re-indexed). imn 'hide' is the reed i and the game-board mn (Y5) with n as complement, and a man behind a wall (coded A5, approximate) as classifier; the next water n is the n of the sḏm·n·f. wi is the chick w with a stroke standing for the seated man. No subject is written after the verb: it is taken as Wepwawet still, 'he has hidden me'; Budge's 'I have hidden myself' would need ·i, which is not there. m-ꜥ·tn 'with you, in your keeping' is the owl m, a second owl drawn with the arm ꜥ in one ligature, and ·tn (t, water n, plural strokes). Budge prints the next three groups apart (àu χemu seku); they are joined here into one word (q re-indexed): iḫmw-sk 'those who do not know perishing'. It is the reed i; ḫ, the owl m and the chick w with the negative arms (coded D35, approximate) and plural strokes as classifiers, the verb ḫm 'not know'; then sk 'perish', s, the cord sk (coded V29, approximate) with k as complement, a star, a stroke and a seated god. The chick after the reed has no place in the word and is not read; taken with Budge as a separate iw, the cry 'O!' or the particle, it hardly changes the sense. The Imperishable Stars are the stars round the pole that never set; the dead hoped to join them.

sentences.l: (iw) · brow(?)-my · (is)-as · Ra · (iw) · face-my · (is)-open
sentences.i: My brow(?) is Ra, and my face is open.
sentences.n: iw, the reed and the chick, opens this and the next statement and is not translated. Budge prints àpt (?) and the seated man as two groups, querying the first; they are joined here as wpt·i (q re-indexed). The first sign is a tall staff with a crossbar and a forked top, coded as the standard R15, approximate (S40 is also possible); then t, a stroke and a small curl taken as the flesh sign (F51, approximate), the classifier of parts of the body, and the seated man ·i, which Budge restores in brackets. The forked top is taken as the horns wp on a staff (the code R15 is only the nearest shape), and àp is how Budge reads the horns wp elsewhere (Àp-uat for wp-wꜣwt in line 2): wpt 'brow, forehead', written with wp, t and the stroke as in Spell 17, here with the flesh sign as well. The sign is not certain, and the reading is doubtful. m rꜥ is the m of predication, 'is (as) Ra': the sun-disc with a stroke and a seated god. ḥr·i 'my face' is the face with its stroke and ·i; wn 'open' is the hatched door (O31) over the low hooked sign (U15), the door here writing the whole word, a stative after its noun. The dead man's body is made divine part by part, and an open face is one that sees and is seen.

sentences.l: (iw) · heart-my · (is)-on · seat-its
sentences.i: My heart is on its seat.
sentences.n: ḥꜣty·i 'my heart' as in Spell 27, the forepart of a lion ḥꜣt with t, two strokes y and the heart as classifier; but the suffix ·i is written with a seated wigged figure (coded A40), the sign of a god, not with the kneeling man. ḥr 'on' is the face with its stroke. st·f 'its seat' is the seat st (Q1) with t as complement, a small house (coded O1, approximate) as classifier, and the viper ·f. A heart on its seat is a heart in its place and at rest, the condition for thought and speech.

sentences.l: utterance-my · know-I
sentences.i: My utterance I know.
sentences.n: Budge prints ṭep and re-à as two groups; they are joined here into one word, tp-rꜣ·i (q re-indexed): the head tp and the mouth rꜣ, each with its stroke, and ·i. tp-rꜣ is 'utterance', literally 'the head (or tip) of the mouth'. rḫ·i 'I know' is the mouth r, the placenta ḫ and the papyrus roll as classifier, with ·i, which Budge restores in brackets: the sḏm·f. The object stands first, as if for emphasis; the order is unusual, and the sense ('I know what I have to say') is a guess. The dead needed the right words at every gate and before every god.

sentences.l: I · (am)-Ra · protecting · him · himself
sentences.i: I am Ra, protecting himself by himself.
sentences.n: ink 'I' (the pot, the basket and the seated man) with a noun after it makes a sentence without a verb, 'I am Ra'; Ra is written with the seated god with the disc on his head (C1) alone. mkt is the owl m, the arm, k and t (Budge: māket, 'verily'); the arm carries no sound here and is a classifier, as in mkt 'protection' in Spell 147. It is taken as mkt, the infinitive of mki 'protect', which ends in t, with sw as its object; the construction is unusual, and the reading is doubtful. sw 'him' is the sedge sw with w as complement, the dependent pronoun as object, and ḏs·f 'himself' is the cobra ḏ, the bolt s and ·f, as in Spell 27. The sun-god, who came into being by himself, needs no other to guard him.

sentences.l: not · shall-be-ignored-I · not · shall-be-robbed-I
sentences.i: I shall not be ignored; I shall not be robbed.
sentences.n: n is the negative arms (coded D35, approximate) alone. With the sḏm·f it denies what is past or always so, but these papyri often write it where nn 'shall not' is meant, and the future is taken here, as the title asks. ḫm 'not know, ignore' is ḫ and the owl m with the negative arms as classifier, the verb of not knowing. The seated man ·i is written before t and the chick w, the tw of the passive sḏm·tw·f, and read after it: 'I shall not be ignored'. ꜥwꜣ 'rob' is the arm ꜥ, the lasso wꜣ (coded V4, approximate) with ꜣ as complement, and the low hooked sign (U15) as the classifier of force, with ·i and tw in the same order (Budge reads the two lines 'not am I made of no effect, not is violence done to me'). To be forgotten or robbed of offerings was to lose one's life in the world below.

sentences.l: lives · for-you · father-your · O-son · of-Nut
sentences.i: Your father lives for you, son of Nut.
sentences.n: Budge prints ānχ-nek as one group; it is split here into ꜥnḫ and n·k (q re-indexed). ꜥnḫ 'live' is the sign ꜥnḫ (S34) with n and ḫ as complements: the sḏm·f, with its noun subject itf·k after the short phrase n·k 'for you' (water n and the basket). itf·k 'your father' is t and the viper f without the reed i, a common short writing, with a seated god as classifier and ·k. sꜣ nwt 'son of Nut' is the pintail duck sꜣ (G39) with its stroke, then nwt, the pot nw, t, the sky and a rearing cobra as classifiers: the one spoken to is Osiris, whose mother is the sky-goddess. The speaker turns from himself to Osiris, and in the next words calls himself his son.

sentences.l: I · (am)-son-your · eldest · see-I · secrets-your
sentences.i: I am your eldest son; I see your secrets.
sentences.n: sꜣ·k 'your son' is the duck with its stroke and ·k. wr 'great, elder' is the swallow wr (G36) with r as complement, a standing man with a staff (coded A21, approximate), the sign of rank, and a seated god as classifiers: sꜣ wr 'the eldest son'. mꜣꜣ·i 'I see' is the eye with the sickle mꜣ (U1) in one ligature, two vultures ꜣ (the first a complement) and ·i, which Budge restores in brackets: the sḏm·f. štꜣ·k 'your secret (things)' is a rectangle crossed by a double line (coded N37, approximate), taken as the sign that writes štꜣ, with t and ꜣ as complements, the papyrus roll, a dotted stroke and ·k; a small straight-sided cup printed under the t (coded W10, approximate) is not explained (Budge: śeta-k). The eldest son is the heir, who may see what is hidden from others.

sentences.l: (iw)-I · have-appeared-I · as · king · of-the-gods
sentences.i: I have appeared in glory as king of the gods.
sentences.n: iw·i is the reed and the chick, with a stroke standing for the seated man ·i. ḫꜥ 'appear in glory' is the hill with the rising sun ḫꜥ (N28) with ꜥ as complement and the papyrus roll; k, the chick w and the seated man write the ending ·kwi of the stative, 'I have appeared' (Budge: χāā-kuà). nswt 'king' is the sedge, t and water n, the sedge written first: nswt nṯrw 'king of the gods', a direct genitive, the flag three times. The verb is used of the sun at dawn and of a king on the day of his crowning.

sentences.l: not · shall-die-I · again · in · the-necropolis
sentences.i: I shall not die again in the necropolis.
sentences.n: The title comes back as a statement, with n as in line 4. mt·i 'I (shall not) die' is written here with the sign m (Aa15), t and the small ring (coded N33, approximate), and ·i. Budge prints em-nem as one group; it is split here into m and nm (q re-indexed): the owl, then the slender rod (coded T34, approximate) and a flat sign with an upright tab (coded U15) over a stroke, where the title had the owl and the papyrus roll. The phrase is read as in the title, and the reading is no more certain. m 'in' is the sign m (Aa15). Spell 44 ends here.

sentences.l: spell · of · not · rotting · in · the-necropolis
sentences.i: Spell for not rotting in the necropolis.
sentences.n: Spell 45 begins. The papyrus writes rꜣ n tmt ḥwꜣ m in red and ẖrt-nṯr in black. ḥwꜣ 'rot, decay' is the wick ḥ, the lasso wꜣ (coded V4, approximate) with ꜣ as complement, and a ringed oval (coded Aa2, approximate), the classifier of swelling and decay (Budge: ḥua): the verb of the noun ḥwꜣw 'rottenness' in Spell 17, here in the negatival complement after tmt. The body had to last for its owner to live on; embalming fought the rot that this spell forbids.

sentences.l: said · by · the-Osiris · Ani · weary-one · (twice) · as · Osiris
sentences.i: Said by the Osiris Ani: O weary one! (Twice.) As Osiris!
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in in red. wrd 'weary, inert' is the swallow wr (G36) with r as complement, the hand d printed lying flat, and a seated man hunched forward (coded A7, approximate), the weary man, as classifier (Budge: urṭ). It is taken as a participle used as a noun, 'weary one', and as a cry said twice (sp sn); a statement, 'I am weary', is also possible. m 'as' is the owl, which Budge restores in brackets. wsir 'Osiris' is written here with the eye first, then the throne st (Q1) and a seated god; the eye and the god are restored by Budge. Wrd-ib, 'Weary of heart', is a name of the dead Osiris, who lies still in death until he is raised.

sentences.l: weary · of-limb · as · Osiris
sentences.i: Weary of limb, as Osiris is!
sentences.n: wrd ꜥt 'weary of limb' is a verb of quality with a noun after it that says in what respect, a common pattern (as wsḫ šnbt 'broad of breast'). wrd has here, after the weary man, a small lying bird (coded G37, approximate), the classifier of what is small or bad; Budge prints the numeral 2 inside the word. ꜥt 'limb' is the arm ꜥ and t, with a small curl taken as the flesh sign (coded F51, approximate) and a stroke (Budge: āt, 'of limbs'). m wsir 'as Osiris' as in the line before, the eye first.

sentences.l: not · shall-be-weary-they · not · shall-rot-they · not · shall-pass-away(?)-they · not · shall-depart(?)-they
sentences.i: They shall not be weary, they shall not rot, they shall not pass away(?), they shall not depart(?).
sentences.n: Four short clauses, each the negative arms n with a sḏm·f, taken as the future as in Spell 44. In the first three the subject is the bolt ·s 'she, it', which looks back to the feminine ꜥt 'limb', taken of the limbs as a whole, 'they' (Budge adds -et in brackets in his transliteration only). wrd·s and ḥwꜣ·s as before. dꜣ is the hand d (printed lying flat), the vulture ꜣ and the walking legs: a verb of going not met before in these parts (Budge: ṭa, 'disappear'); the meaning is a guess. bn is the leg b and water n, again with the walking legs (Budge: ben, 'depart'); its subject is the bolt with t, ·st, a form of the suffix 'it, they' found in later texts. Both verbs are doubtful, but what the clauses ask is plain: that the body stay whole and in its place.

sentences.l: let-be-done · for-me · as · I · (am)-Osiris
sentences.i: Let this be done for me, as I am Osiris.
sentences.n: Budge prints àru-nà as one group; it is split here into irw and n·i (q re-indexed). irw is the eye ir, the chick w and a stroke: the passive sḏm of iri 'do', with the w that the passive sometimes shows, here as a wish. n·i 'for me' is water n and the seated man. mi 'like, as' is the milk-jug mi (W19) with i as complement and the papyrus roll (Budge: mà). mi with a sentence after it, ink wsir 'I am Osiris', gives 'as I am Osiris'. What is wished for the body of Osiris is wished for the dead man who bears his name.

sentences.l: if · is-known · spell · this · not · rots-he · in · the-necropolis · Osiris
sentences.i: If this spell is known, he shall not rot in the necropolis. Osiris (…).
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir rḫ rꜣ pn n ḥwꜣ·f m in red; ẖrt-nṯr and wsir are in black. ir 'if' is the reed and the mouth; rḫ (the mouth, the placenta ḫ and the papyrus roll) is the passive sḏm, 'is known', with rꜣ pn 'this spell' as its subject, as at the end of Spell 58. ḥwꜣ·f 'he rots' has here the papyrus roll after the ringed oval, and the viper ·f. ẖrt-nṯr is written out: the flag, the block ẖr (T28) over r and t, and the hills as classifier, where the title has the short group. The last word, wsir, stands alone: it may be the start of 'the Osiris Ani' with the name left unwritten, and it is given as it stands. Spell 45 ends here.

sentences.l: spell · of · not · perishing · being · alive · in · the-necropolis
sentences.i: Spell for not perishing and for being alive in the necropolis.
sentences.n: Spell 46 begins. The papyrus writes rꜣ n tmt skt wnn ꜥnḫw in red and m ẖrt-nṯr in black. skt is s, the cord sk (coded V29, approximate; printed like the twisted wick) with k as complement, t, and the small lying bird (coded G37, approximate), the classifier of what is bad: sk 'perish', the verb of iḫmw-sk in Spell 44, with t as the negatival complement after tmt (Budge: sekt). wnn is the hare wn with water n as complement and a second n: the infinitive of wnn 'be', standing beside tmt, not under it, 'and for being'. ꜥnḫw 'alive' is the sign ꜥnḫ with n and ḫ and the chick w, the stative after wnn (Budge: ānχu).

sentences.l: said · by · the-Osiris · Ani · O · youths · of-Shu · (twice) · of-the-Duat(?) · who-have-power · over · fillet-his · among · the-Henmemet
sentences.i: Said by the Osiris Ani: O youths of Shu (Twice.), of the Duat(?), who have power over his fillet among the Henmemet!
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in in red. i 'O' is the reed with a man raising his hands to his face (A2). ḥwnw 'youths, children' is the wick ḥ, the hare wn with n, the pot nw and the coil w repeating its sounds, and a seated child with hand to mouth (coded A17, approximate), the kneeling man and a stroke as classifiers (Budge: ḥunnu). šw 'Shu', the god of the air, is the feather šw (H6) with w and a seated god; sp sn, restored in brackets by Budge, repeats the call. dwꜣt is the star dwꜣ (N14) with ꜣ and a small house (coded O1, approximate) as classifier, without t: taken as the Duat, the world below, in a direct genitive; Budge's 'place of the dawn' (dwꜣ is also 'morning') is possible, and the reading is doubtful. sḫm 'have power over' (with m) is the sceptre sḫm (S42) with s, m and ḫ as complements and a small bird with arms (coded G24, approximate) as classifier: a participle, 'who have power'. sšd·f is the bolt s, two looped cords (coded V6, approximate) with the hand d between them, and ·f: taken as sšd 'fillet, headband' (Budge: 'diadem'). m ḥnmmt 'among the Henmemet' is the disc with falling rays (coded N8, approximate), which writes ḥnmmt, with m twice as complement (the owl and the sign m), t, the kneeling man, a seated god and a stroke as classifiers (Budge: hamemet). The ḥnmmt are a class of beings who live in the sun's light; whose fillet is meant is not said, perhaps Ra's.

sentences.l: have-hastened(?)-I · moving-about · (as)-Osiris
sentences.i: I have hastened(?); I move about as Osiris.
sentences.n: wn·n·i is the hare wn with n, the walking legs as classifier, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·i: taken as wn 'hasten, hurry', a verb of motion spelt like wn 'open', 'I have hastened' (Budge: 'may I rise up'); the sense is doubtful. wnwn 'move about, roam' is the same group twice with the walking legs once: the reduplicated verb, here without a written subject. No m 'as' is written before wsir; Budge supplies 'like'. The word may instead be the start of 'the Osiris Ani' with the name left out, as at the end of Spell 45. Spell 46 ends here.

sentences.l: spell · of · not · entering · into · the-block · of-the-god
sentences.i: Spell for not going in to the slaughter-block of the god.
sentences.n: Spell 50 begins. The papyrus writes rꜣ n tmt ꜥq r in red and nmmt nṯr in black; the water n of n is restored in brackets by Budge. ꜥq 'enter' is the arm ꜥ (printed as a flat line with an upright tab), the triangle q (N29) and the walking legs, the negatival complement after tmt; ꜥq r 'enter into'. nmmt 'the block' is a domed block with a knife laid across it (coded T29), which writes the word alone (Budge: nemmat). Budge prints the flag and the seated god in the same group and takes them as classifiers; they are split off here as nṯr 'god', the flag with the seated god as in ḥtp-nṯr at the end of Spell 93 A, in a direct genitive: nmmt nṯr 'the block of the god', the slaughter-block of the gods. There the enemies of the gods were cut up; the dead man must not come to it.

sentences.l: said · by · the-Osiris · Ani · (iw) · is-knit · for-me · nape-my · in · heaven · the-keeper(?) · of-the-earth · by · Ra
sentences.i: Said by the Osiris Ani: My nape is knit together for me in heaven by Ra, the keeper(?) of the earth.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in in red; in is written here with the reed and water n. Budge prints θesu-nà as one group; it is split here into ṯs·w and n·i (q re-indexed). ṯs 'tie, knit together' is the girdle knot ṯs (S24) with the coil w under it and the low hooked sign (U15) as classifier: the passive sḏm with its w, 'is tied'. ḥꜣ·i 'my nape, the back of my head' is the papyrus clump ḥꜣ (M16) with ꜣ as complement, a small head (coded D1, approximate) and a stroke as classifiers, and ·i: the noun from which the preposition ḥꜣ 'behind' comes. m pt 'in heaven' is the sign m and the sky. iry is the reed, the mouth r and two strokes y, with a seated wrapped man holding a stick (coded A47, approximate), the sign of a guard, and the papyrus roll: taken as iry 'keeper', with tꜣ 'the earth' (the strip of land, coded N16, approximate) after it. in 'by' names the agent, and rꜥ 'Ra' is r and the arm ꜥ with the seated god with the disc. How iry tꜣ stands in the sentence is not clear: it may be a title of Ra, as taken here, or 'what belongs to the earth'. The knitting of neck to head is what the slaughter-block would undo.

sentences.l: given(?) · (on)-the-day · of · making-firm · raising-up-my · from · weariness · on · the-two-legs · (on)-day · that · (?) · of · cutting-off · the-hair
sentences.i: It was given(?) on the day of making firm my raising up from weariness upon the legs, on that day … of the cutting off of the hair.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ṯsnw·i; read ṯsw·i. rdit is the mouth r, t and the arm (D36, no loaf in the hand): the infinitive of rdi 'give', here without a subject, perhaps as a heading, and rendered 'it was given'; the form and the sense are doubtful (Budge: 'it hath been granted'). hrw 'day' is the courtyard h (O4), r, w, the sun and a stroke, an adverb of time without a preposition, as often. smnt 'making firm' is the bolt s, the game-board mn with n, a tall hooked staff (coded S38, approximate; a classifier not identified), t and the papyrus roll: the infinitive of smn 'make firm, establish', after the genitive n. ṯsw·i is the girdle knot ṯs with water n printed under it, the coil w, the low hooked sign and ·i; the water n has no place in the word and is not read (Budge has none), and ṯs is taken in its sense 'raise up', 'my raising up'. r nnyw 'from weariness' is two rushes and two water n's (nn), two reeds y and the chick w, with the weary man (coded A7, approximate), the small bird and plural strokes: nni 'be weary, inert', the state of the dead before they are raised. ḥr mnty 'upon the two legs' is the game-board mn with n, t, two strokes and two legs, the dual of mnt 'thigh, leg'. After pfy 'that' (the stool p, the viper f, two strokes) Budge prints at the head of line 3 a sign he does not read and does not translate (coded R3, approximate: a bar on a small foot with two knobbed uprights); it is joined here to pfy as an unread sign (q re-indexed). The genitive nt that follows is feminine, which hrw is not: the unread sign may be a feminine noun we cannot now read. ḥsq 'cut off' is the wick ḥ, s and the triangle q (N29), with the knife and the low hooked sign as classifiers. smꜣt is the lung and windpipe smꜣ (coded F36) with a stroke, m, t and hanging tresses as classifier: a word for the hair of the head (Budge: samet). The day of cutting the hair is not explained; cutting the hair was a sign of mourning.

sentences.l: (iw) · has-been-tied · the-vertebra · of-nape-my · by · Seth · (and)-the-Ennead · of-the-gods · in · strength-their · first
sentences.i: The vertebra of my nape has been tied by Seth and the Ennead of the gods, in their first strength.
sentences.n: ṯs 'tie' is the girdle knot with s as complement and the low hooked sign: the passive sḏm, 'has been tied'. ṯst 'vertebra, backbone' is the knot with t and a stroke, the noun from ṯs (Budge: θest, 'the vertebrae'), in a direct genitive with ḥꜣ·i 'my nape', written here without the vulture. in 'by' names the agents. stẖ 'Seth' is the bolt and a hatched rectangle (coded N37, approximate, by house ruling) with a seated god: the sign under the bolt stands for the rest of the name. psḏt nṯrw 'the Ennead of the gods' is the loaf (X6), which writes psḏt, with t, and the flag three times; no 'and' is written between Seth and the Ennead. m wsr·s tpy 'in their first strength': wsr 'strength' is the head and neck of an animal wsr (F12) with s and r and the low hooked sign; ·s 'her, its' looks back to the Ennead, a feminine noun; tpy 'first' is the head tp with a stroke and two strokes y; Budge prints the numeral 4 inside wsr·s. That Seth, the murderer of Osiris, should tie the dead man's neck is striking; the spell does not explain it.

sentences.l: not · shall-come-into-being · strife
sentences.i: No strife shall come into being.
sentences.n: n with ḫpr 'come into being' (the scarab ḫpr with r as complement): a sḏm·f with its noun subject after it, again taken as the future. ḫnnw 'strife, disturbance' is a sign like an oar crossing a container (coded P8, approximate), taken as the sign ḫn, two water n's, the pot nw and the chick w, with the low hooked sign and plural strokes as classifiers (Budge: χennu, 'separation'). The reading of the first sign is doubtful.

sentences.l: may-preserve-you · me · from · the-slayer · of-father-my
sentences.i: May you keep me safe from the slayer of my father.
sentences.n: swḏꜣ 'make sound, keep whole' is the bolt s, the chick w and the fire-drill ḏꜣ (coded U28, approximate) with ꜣ as complement and the papyrus roll, then ·tn 'you' (t, water n, plural strokes): the sḏm·f as a wish, said to the gods. Budge prints a single stroke in brackets after it, his restoration, and reads à 'me'; it is split off here as wi, the object pronoun, for which the stroke stands (q re-indexed). m 'from' is the owl. smꜣ 'slayer' is the bolt s and the sickle mꜣ (U1) rising over the vulture ꜣ, with the knife and the low hooked sign as classifiers: the participle 'who slays'. itf·i 'my father' is the reed, t and the viper f, with the seated man as classifier and again as ·i. The slayer of the father is Seth, who killed Osiris; the speaker is now in the place of Horus, the son who avenged him.

sentences.l: I · (am-the-one-who)-took · the-Two-Lands
sentences.i: I am the one who took possession of the Two Lands.
sentences.n: ink with a participle after it: 'I am the one who …'. iṯ 'take, seize' is written as in Spell 27: the tether (coded V13, approximate) with the walking legs, then t written for ṯ and the low hooked sign; Budge prints the numeral 5 inside the word. tꜣwy 'the Two Lands', Egypt, is the strip of land twice, each with two slanting strokes: the dual. To take the Two Lands is the claim of Horus as king.

sentences.l: has-been-tied · vertebra-my · by · Nut · seeing · occasion-her · first · she-who-sees · right-order · not · had-been-born · the-gods · in · forms
sentences.i: My vertebra has been tied by Nut, who saw at her first occasion, who sees right order, when the gods had not yet been born in their forms.
sentences.n: ṯs·w 'has been tied' is the girdle knot with the coil w, over the bolt s and the low hooked sign: the passive sḏm with w, as in line 1; ṯst·i 'my vertebra' has the seated man ·i. in 'by' is written with the reed first, then the sign in (coded W25, approximate). mꜣꜣ is the eye with the sickle and two vultures; mꜣꜣt adds t. Both are taken as participles describing Nut, the second with the feminine ending, the first without it; mꜣꜣ may instead be the infinitive, 'seeing'. sp·s tpy 'her first occasion' is the bolt s, the stool p and the threshing floor sp as classifier, the bolt ·s 'her', and tpy 'first' (the head tp, the stool p as complement, two strokes y): the first time, the beginning of the world. mꜣꜥt 'right order' is the sickle mꜣ, the arm ꜥ, t, the plinth mꜣꜥ (Aa11) and a roll (coded Y1, approximate) over plural strokes. n is the negative arms with water n as complement; with msi 'bear, be born' (the three fox-skins ms with s, and a seated woman giving birth, coded B3, approximate, as classifier) it is the passive in the past, 'the gods had not (yet) been born'. ꜥšmw is the arm ꜥ (printed flat; Budge reads a), the pool š (coded N37, approximate), the owl m, the chick w and a falcon with a flail (G6) as classifier: ꜥšm 'form, image of a god' (Budge: aśemu, 'visible forms'). Nut, the sky, was there before the gods she bore; the dead man is knit together by the oldest of powers.

sentences.l: I · (am)-Penty
sentences.i: I am Penty.
sentences.n: pnty is the stool p, water n, t and two strokes y with a seated god as classifier (Budge: Penti): the name of a god not met before in these parts. It may be a nisba, 'he who belongs to …', but its sense is unknown.

sentences.l: (iw)-I · as · heir · of-the-gods · great · the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani · true-of-voice
sentences.i: I am the great heir of the gods, the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice.
sentences.n: iw·i m 'I am (as)': the particle iw with ·i (the seated man), and the m of predication. iwꜥ 'heir' is the young animal iw (E9), the arm ꜥ and a leg-bone with meat (coded F44, approximate) as classifier (Budge: āuā). ꜥꜣ 'great' is the column ꜥꜣ (coded O29, approximate) with ꜥ and ꜣ as complements, the papyrus roll and a stroke; it is singular, so it is taken with iwꜥ, 'the great heir', not with nṯrw. wsir sš ꜣny mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice' follows as the speaker's name: the palette sš (Y3), and mꜣꜥ-ḫrw written short, the plinth and the oar without the sickle. Spell 50 ends here.

sentences.l: spell · of · not · letting · be-ferried · a-man · to · the-east · in · the-necropolis
sentences.i: Spell for not letting a man be ferried to the east in the necropolis.
sentences.n: Spell 93 begins. The papyrus writes rꜣ n tmt rdit ḏꜣ·tw in red, s in black, r iꜣbt m in red, and ẖrt-nṯr in black. rdit 'letting' as in Spell 27: the mouth r, t and the arm (no loaf). ḏꜣ·tw is the fire-drill ḏꜣ (coded U28, approximate) with ꜣ as complement, a boat-like sign on a low base (coded P1, approximate; the sign is unsure) and the low hooked sign as classifiers, and the tw of the passive: 'letting (a man) be ferried', from ḏꜣi 'cross, ferry over'. s 'a man' is the bolt, a stroke and the seated man. iꜣbt 'the east' is the standard of the east iꜣb (R15) with b and t. The east, where the sun rises, is here the place of the festivals of the rebels, as the spell goes on to say, and the dead man must not be carried there.

sentences.l: said · by · the-Osiris · Ani · O · phallus · this · of · Ra · which-moves(?) · destroys-it · strife
sentences.i: Said by the Osiris Ani: O this phallus of Ra, which moves(?) and destroys strife!
sentences.n: The papyrus writes nwy; read pwy. ḏd in is in red; in is the reed and water n. i 'O' is the reed with a man raising one arm (coded A26, approximate). ḥnnw 'phallus' is the wick ḥ, a long blade with a crosspiece (coded U7, approximate) where the plant ḥn is expected, water n, the pot nw and the chick w, with the phallus (D52) as classifier (Budge: ḥennu); in line 6 of the next spell the same word has the plant ḥn (M2). The demonstrative is printed with the pot nw where the stool p should be (Budge: nui, 'that'); the same phrase, ḥnnw pwy n rꜥ, is written with the stool in the next spell, and the sense allows only pwy 'this'. n rꜥ 'of Ra': water n and the seated god with the disc. nwd is water n, the adze nw (coded U19, approximate) with the pot nw and the chick w, then a long rounded bar (coded Y1, approximate) and the walking legs, both restored by Budge in brackets: the bar is taken as the flat hand d, as Budge reads it (ennuṭ, 'advancing'), and the word as nwd 'turn, move', a participle; the reading is doubtful. ḥḏ·f is the mace ḥḏ (T3) with a cobra ḏ wound round it, the crossed sticks and the small bird as classifiers, and ·f: ḥḏ 'damage, destroy', a sḏm·f, 'it destroys'. ḫnnw 'strife' as in Spell 50. The phallus of Ra is the sun's power to beget, called on here against disorder.

sentences.l: come-into-being · things · inert · for · a-million · through(?) · Babi
sentences.i: Things that are inert for a million (years) come into being through(?) Babi.
sentences.n: ḫpr 'come into being' with its noun subject ḫt 'things' (the placenta ḫ, t, a roll and a stroke). nnw 'inert' is the rushes and water n's as in Spell 50, here with the pot nw and the chick w and no reeds, and the same classifiers: taken as a participle of nni after its noun, 'which are inert'. m ḥḥ 'for a million' is the owl and the god Heh with raised arms (C11), a stroke and plural strokes: the number used for endless time, 'for millions (of years)'. m bby is the sign m (Aa15), then the leg b and the reed, twice, and a seated god: Babi, the savage baboon god, written without the vulture (Budge: Bàbà). How m bby joins the sentence is not clear; 'through' or 'from Babi' is a guess.

sentences.l: am-strong-I · thereby · more-than · the-strong · am-mighty-I · thereby · more-than · the-mighty
sentences.i: By it I am stronger than the strong; by it I am mightier than the mighty.
sentences.n: wsr 'be strong' is the head and neck of an animal (F12) with s and r and the low hooked sign, and ·i: the sḏm·f of a verb of quality, 'I am strong'. im 'thereby, by it' is the reed and the owl: the preposition m with no noun after it, pointing back to something named before, perhaps the phallus of Ra. r 'than' after a verb of quality makes the comparison, 'strong beyond'. wsrw 'the strong' has a small bird with arms (coded G24, approximate) and a stroke as classifiers, a plural with its w not written. sḫm·i 'I am mighty' and sḫmw 'the mighty' are the sceptre sḫm with m, in the same pattern.

sentences.l: now · not · shall-one-ferry
sentences.i: Now no one shall ferry (me).
sentences.n: ir 'now, as for' is the reed and the mouth, the particle that sets up what follows. nn 'shall not' is the negative arms (coded D35, approximate) with water n, the negative of the future with the sḏm·f. ḏꜣ·tw is written as in the title, the classifier here a low base carrying a small sprawling shape (coded P1, approximate; a duckling or the fire-drill is also possible). No suffix follows the tw, so it is impersonal, 'one shall not ferry', and the one not ferried, 'me', is understood from what follows (Budge: 'I shall not be conveyed').

sentences.l: now · not · shall-be-carried-off-I · to · the-east · to · perform · the-festivals · of-the-rebels · there · with · cutting · evil · with · (ḥst) · with · binding(?) · of-the-horns
sentences.i: Now I shall not be carried off to the east to perform the festivals of the rebels there, with evil cutting, with (ḥst?), with binding(?) of the horns.
sentences.n: ir again, and n, the negative arms alone, here for nn as in Spell 44. iṯ 'seize, carry off' is the tether (coded V13, approximate) on a small stand, t for ṯ and the low hooked sign, with ·i written before the tw of the passive and read after it, as in Spell 44. iꜣbtt 'the east' has here two t's and the hills as classifier. r irt 'to perform' is r with the infinitive irt, the eye and t. ḥbw 'festivals' is the wick ḥ and the leg b with the alabaster basin ḥb (W3), the sun and plural strokes. sbiw 'rebels' is s, b and the reed, with a throw-stick (coded T14, approximate), a small ring (coded N33, approximate) and plural strokes: the enemies of the sun. im 'there' is the reed and the owl. Three phrases with m 'with' follow. šꜥd ḏwt 'evil cutting': šꜥd is the pool š (coded N37, approximate), the arm ꜥ and the hand d, with a stem with side-shoots (coded M3, approximate), the knife and a stroke as classifiers (Budge: śāṭ, 'gashings'); ḏwt 'evil' is the mountain ḏw with t, w, the small bird and plural strokes. ḥst is the wick ḥ, the jar ḥs (coded W14, approximate), s, t and the walking legs: a word not known, and Budge's 'shutting in on every side' is a guess. nwḥt is water n, the adze nw (coded U19, approximate) with the pot and the chick, ḥ, t and two strokes, taken as nwḥ 'bind with a rope', 'binding'; ḥnwty is the two horns written alone (F16 twice), read with Budge as the dual of ḥnwt 'horn' (Budge: ḥennuti; ꜥbwy 'the two horns' is also possible). Budge has 'goring by the horns', and the reading is doubtful. A beast for sacrifice was led and bound by its horns: at the festivals of the rebels the enemies of Ra are slaughtered like cattle, and the dead man must not be taken there as a victim.

sentences.l: not · shall-fall(?)-you · swallowing(?) · fish · with · doing · goring(?) · to-me
sentences.i: You shall not fall(?) … swallowing(?) fish … with goring(?) done to me.
sentences.n: The clause is obscure, and Budge leaves its first part untranslated. nn with ḫr·k: ḫ and r with the falling man (coded A15, approximate), and ·k: 'you shall not fall'; who is spoken to is not said. ꜥm 'swallow' is the arm ꜥ, which Budge restores in brackets, the owl m and the man with hand to mouth; rmw 'fish' is the mouth r, the owl m, the chick w, a fish (K1) and plural strokes (Budge: remu); Budge prints the numeral 5 inside the word. Budge prints tebu-nà as one group; it is split here into tbw and n·i (q re-indexed). m irt tbw n·i 'with doing tbw to me': irt is the infinitive of iri; tbw is t, the leg b and the chick w with no classifier, taken as db 'gore, butt', the verb written with the horns in the next spell, here with t for d (Budge: 'goring'). The words do not join into a clear sentence; the dots in the translation mark the breaks in sense, not missing words (Budge's dotted line is in his English only). Spell 93 ends here.

sentences.l: another · spell
sentences.i: Another spell.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky rꜣ in red. ky 'another' is the basket k with two reeds y; here it comes before its noun (Budge: ki re, 'another chapter'). What follows is another spell to the same end as Spell 93, numbered 93 A.

sentences.l: now · not · shall-be-done · thing · any · evil · against-me · by · the-rebels · with · binding(?) · of-the-horns
sentences.i: Now nothing evil shall be done against me by the rebels, nor with binding(?) of the horns.
sentences.n: ir nn 'now … shall not' as in Spell 93. ir·tw is the eye and t with the chick, the tw of the passive: with nn, 'shall not be done'. ḫt nbt bint 'any evil thing': ḫt 'thing' (the placenta ḫ, t, a roll and a stroke), nbt 'any' (the basket nb with t, feminine to agree with ḫt) and bint 'evil' (the leg b, the reed, water n, t and the small bird). r·i 'against me' is the mouth and the seated man. m sbiw 'by the rebels' (here a small dot printed in the s is not coded) and m nwḥt ḥnwty as in Spell 93, with the same doubts.

sentences.l: not · shall-swallow · then · phallus · this · of · Ra · the-head · of · Osiris
sentences.i: This phallus of Ra shall not, then, swallow the head of Osiris.
sentences.n: nn with the sḏm·f ꜥm 'swallow', which has here, between the owl and the man with hand to mouth, a tall stem with a crossbar near its foot and a two-horned knob on top (coded F35, approximate, as if inverted; M13 also possible), not explained. irf 'then' is the mouth and the viper, r·f, the enclitic particle (Budge: eref, 'therefore'). ḥnnw 'phallus' is the wick ḥ and the plant ḥn (coded M2, approximate) with n, the pot nw and the chick w, without the phallus as classifier. pwy 'this' is the stool p, the chick w and two reeds. ḏꜣḏꜣ 'head' is the fire-drill ḏꜣ (coded U28, approximate) twice and a head in profile (Budge: t'at'a). The phallus is taken as the subject and the head of Osiris as the object; read as a passive, 'shall not be swallowed', the two would stand side by side. Either way the body of Osiris, head and member, is kept whole.

sentences.l: see-I · have-come-I · to · fields-my · reap-I · gods-my · answer-they · with-me
sentences.i: See, I have come to my fields; I reap, and my gods answer with me.
sentences.n: istw·i is the reed, s, t and the chick, the particle ist 'see, now', with the seated man ·i after it (Budge: àstu-à); a dependent pronoun would be expected there, and the form is unusual. Budge prints the numeral 7 inside the word. ii·kw 'I have come' is the reed with legs ii (M18) with i as complement, two strokes and the walking legs, then k and w: the stative ending ·kwi without its last sign. r ꜣḥt·i 'to my fields' is the vulture ꜣ, ḥ and t, with a small wedge (coded N21, approximate) and a stroke as classifiers, and ·i. ḥsq·i 'I cut' is the verb of Spell 50 with the knife, taken of reaping in the fields (Budge: 'I reap'). nṯrw·i 'my gods' is the flag three times and ·i. wšb·sn 'they answer' is the chick w, a rectangle with two diagonal strokes (coded N37, approximate, for š) over a small cross (coded Z9, approximate), the leg b, restored by Budge in brackets, and the man with hand to mouth, the classifier of speech, with ·sn (Budge: us[eb]-sen, 'speak they'). im·i 'with me' is the reed and the owl with ·i. The dead man works his own fields in the world below, and the gods take his part.

sentences.l: not · shall-gore-you · then · Ra-Khepri
sentences.i: You shall not, then, gore Ra-Khepri.
sentences.n: n, the negative arms alone, with db·k 'you shall gore': the hand d printed lying flat, the leg b, the two horns as classifier and ·k (Budge: ṭeb-k, 'pierce thou'); Budge prints the numeral 8 inside the word. irf 'then' as before. rꜥ-ḫpri is the seated god with the disc, then the scarab ḫpr with r and the reed i and a seated god: Ra-Khepri, the sun as the scarab that comes into being at dawn (Budge: Rā-χeperà). He is taken as the object; he may instead be the one spoken to, 'O Ra-Khepri'. The horned one spoken to as 'you' is not named.

sentences.l: not · shall-come-into-being · then · then · sickness · in · the-eye · of-Atum · not · shall-be-destroyed-it
sentences.i: Then no sickness shall come into being in the eye of Atum; it shall not be destroyed.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḥbmt·f; read ḥtm·f. n with ḫpr, and two particles after the verb: kꜣ, the basket k, the vulture ꜣ and the man with hand to mouth, the particle kꜣ 'then, so', which looks to the future, and irf 'then' (Budge gives the two one rendering, 'in very truth'). bnnwt is the leg b, two water n's, t and the chick w, with a ringed oval (coded Aa2, approximate), the classifier of swelling and disease, and plural strokes: a word for sickness, not met before in these parts (Budge: benentu). m irt itm 'in the eye of Atum': irt as before, and itm 'Atum' written without the reed, t, the sledge tm (U15) and a seated god (Budge: Tmu). In ḥtm 'be destroyed' the second sign, an upright with a foot (coded D58, approximate), has no place and is not read, perhaps a misprinted sign; Budge prints the numeral 9 after it. m and t follow, the t written after the m and read before it, then a long-necked bird (coded G27, approximate), the small bird and ·f: 'it shall not be destroyed', the eye. The eye of the sun-god is his power in the world; its sickness would darken it.

sentences.l: not · shall-be-robbed-I · not · shall-be-ferried-I · to · the-east · to · perform · the-festivals · of-the-rebels · against(?)-me · evil
sentences.i: I shall not be robbed; I shall not be ferried to the east to perform the festivals of the rebels against(?) me, evil things.
sentences.n: n ꜥwꜣ·tw·i 'I shall not be robbed' as in Spell 44, but the cord here is a looped one (coded V6, approximate), printed after the vulture, where the lasso wꜣ stood there (Budge: 'let be made an end of me'). nn ḏꜣ·tw·i 'I shall not be ferried' is the verb of the title with ·i written before the tw and read after it. r iꜣbtt r irt ḥbw sbiw as in Spell 93; where that has im 'there', this has im·i, with the seated man, 'in me, against me' (Budge supplies '[hostile] to me'). ḏwt 'evil' (the mountain ḏw with t, w and the small bird) stands after it alone, taken as 'evil things' in apposition; the construction is doubtful.

sentences.l: not · shall-be-done · cutting · on-me · evil
sentences.i: No cutting shall be done on me, nothing evil.
sentences.n: nn ir·tw 'shall not be done' is the eye with the mouth r as complement and the tw of the passive. šꜥd 'cutting' as in Spell 93. im·i 'in me, on me' has the seated man restored in brackets by Budge. ḏwt 'evil' again stands after it, here with plural strokes.

sentences.l: not · (is)-ferrying-my · to · the-east
sentences.i: There shall be no ferrying of me to the east.
sentences.n: Here the verb is written with the fire-drill ḏꜣ and ꜣ, two reeds y and t, the boat-like sign and the low hooked sign, and ·i, with no w: ḏꜣyt·i, the infinitive of ḏꜣi with its t, and the suffix as its object, 'my ferrying' (Budge: t'ait-à). nn with a noun is 'there is no …', 'there shall be no ferrying of me'. Read as ḏꜣ·t(w)·i, the passive of the lines before, the sense is the same.

sentences.l: the-Osiris · the-scribe · accountant · of-the-god's-offerings · of · the-gods · all · Ani · true-of-voice · true-of-voice · good · possessor · of-honour
sentences.i: The Osiris, the accounting scribe of the god's offerings of all the gods, Ani, true of voice, true of voice, good, possessor of honour.
sentences.n: The papyrus names Ani with his titles at the end of the second spell. sš ḥsb 'accounting scribe' is the palette and ḥsb, here a ringed oval (coded Aa2, approximate) over a roll (Y1). Budge prints ḥetep and neter as two groups; they are joined here as ḥtp-nṯr 'god's offerings' (q re-indexed): the offering-mat ḥtp (R4) with t and p, and the flag with a seated god. n nṯrw nbw 'of all the gods': water n, the flag three times, and the basket nb with plural strokes, 'all', agreeing with the plural. mꜣꜥ-ḫrw is written twice: first short, the plinth and the oar; then in full, the sickle mꜣ curving round the plinth, the arm ꜥ, the oar, the chick w and the man with hand to mouth (Budge: 'triumphant with victory'). The repetition may be a slip of the pen or the phrase mꜣꜥ-ḫrw m mꜣꜥ-ḫrw with the m left out; it is translated as it stands. nfr 'good' is the heart and windpipe nfr (F35) with f and r. nb imꜣḫ 'possessor of honour' is the basket and the spine imꜣḫ (coded F39, approximate) with its stroke: the honoured state of the blessed dead. The part ends here; below the rule Budge begins Spell 43.
